subject: german
title: Describing Outfits
welcome_lead: Combining colour + clothing to describe outfits.
meta_desc: KS3 German: adjective + noun, simple outfits.
final_note: Combine colour and clothing for full descriptions.

walkthroughs.body_html: Ich trage (I wear), du tragst (you wear), er/sie tragt (he/she wears). 'Was tragst du heute?' = 'What are you wearing today?'
Before a noun, adjectives add endings: 'ein rotes T-Shirt' (a red T-shirt). After 'ist' nothing changes: 'das T-Shirt ist rot'. The 'after ist' version is easier — use that first.
To say 'favourite' add Lieblings- as a prefix. Mein Lieblingspulli = my favourite jumper. Meine Lieblingsfarbe = my favourite colour.

mcqs.q: When addressing a stranger or someone older formally, which 'you' do you use?
options: Sie (always capitalised, formal singular and plural).

mcqs.q: What case does 'helfen' (to help) require for its object?
What is the difference between 'ich will' and 'ich möchte'?
options: Ich will = I want (strong, direct); ich möchte = I would like (polite).
